newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos says Spratlys should be in sea of friendship.
newsitem.headline: Ramos says Spratlys should be in sea of friendship.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos on Tuesday urged joint efforts by China and the Philippines to turn the South China Sea into a zone of cooperation and not confrontation.
Ramos, hosting a dinner for Chinese President Jiang Zemin, also stressed the need to remove irritants in relations between China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).
Jiang attended Monday's trade summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum at nearby Subic Bay freeport and began on Tuesday a three-day state visit to the Philippines.
China is locked in a six-nation dispute over ownership of the potentially oil-rich Spratly Islands in the South China Sea.
The area is claimed wholly or in part by China, Taiwan, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Brunei. The latter four countries are partners in the seven-nation ASEAN.

"We must intensify our efforts and transform that sea from waters of contention to an area of cooperation and mutual benefit," Ramos said, according to the text of his dinner speech released in advance by the presidential palace.

Ramos, referring to relations between ASEAN and China, added: "To insure our regional partnership become strong and durable, Mr President, I believe our governments must intensify their efforts to remove the minor irritants in our friendly relationships."
Jiang, in his own prepared speech, said it would take decades "for China...to achieve modernisation".
He added: "China's development will only contribute to peace and development in the region and the world at large, instead of posing a threat to any country."
Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Shen Guo Fang told a news briefing China's focus at this time was to modernise its economy.
"And even if China is developed in the future, China will not threaten other countries," he said.
Shen said Jiang and Ramos agreed to shelve their differences over the Spratlys and that "both sides should work for new ways for the common development" of the area.
Ramos told Jiang the two countries' leadership should have a vision "longer than the Great Wall of China", Shen said.
Jiang told Ramos: "A friend is good when new but it is better when he becomes an old friend."
Jiang said he considered Ramos "an old friend".

Jiang's visit was highlighted by the signing of several accords, including a memorandum of agreement signed by China's Shanghai Electric Corp to grant a $180 million suppliers' credit to the Philippines' Magellan Utilities Development Corp.
The credit was partly to finance construction of a 300-megawatt power plant in Batangas, south of Manila.

A consortium led by China's Harbin Power Engineering Co Ltd signed a build-operate-transfer contract with the Philippines' National Power Corp for a 200-megawatt coal-fired power plant in the southern island of Mindanao.
